topSpeedMPS.citation: Zero published on-ice youth data exists below age 9 (docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md). Linear extrapolation from the U11 real anchor (7.60 m/s, PMC11358090) using the 0.4865 m/s-per-year growth rate averaged across the four real U11-U18 data points (docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md), projected down to age 6.

accel0to10mS.citation: Same extrapolation method as topSpeedMPS, applied to the U11 anchor's 10m acceleration time (derived from PMC11358090's 6.1m split), age 6.

avgAccelMPS2.citation: Computed from THIS profile's own displayed accel0to10mS (2.12s) via kinematics (a = 2d/t^2, d=10m): 20/2.12^2 = 4.45. Tagged derived-from-estimate, not derived-from-citation, because accel0to10mS itself is an engineering estimate for this band, not a citation -- the derivation is real arithmetic, but what it's derived FROM isn't measured data. (Corrected 2026-07-30: an earlier version stored 4.43, computed from an unrounded intermediate value rather than the number actually shown in this file, so it didn't reproduce from the displayed inputs -- caught by adversarial review.)

turningRadiusM.citation: No published turning-radius figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (0.6 * avgAccelMPS2) = 5.654^2 / (0.6*4.45) -- the 0.6 factor assumes lateral/edge turning acceleration is roughly 60% of straight-line push acceleration, a documented simplifying assumption, not measured.

stoppingDistanceM.citation: No published stopping-distance figure exists at any age. Estimated as v^2 / (2 * avgAccelMPS2) = 5.654^2 / (2*4.45), assuming braking capability comparable to acceleration capability -- no direct braking data exists.

reactionDelayS.citation: No ice-hockey or youth-hockey reaction-time study exists at any age. 250-350ms range built from adult non-hockey athlete proxy data (PMC11207928, decomposed perceptual-motor + choice-task components) per docs/scenario-engine/physics-sourcing.md. Applied flat across all age bands rather than inventing an age curve the research doesn't support -- Der & Deary 2006 found under-18s sit at or slightly above young-adult baseline, not faster, so no downward scaling for younger bands is applied.

passSpeedMPS.citation: No youth ice-hockey pass-velocity study exists (the one youth shot-speed study found, MDPI Biomechanics 2023, is rink hockey -- a different sport -- and is excluded). Estimated as a fraction of the U18 reference (18 m/s, itself well below the cited adult 70mph+ shot lower bound since passes are gentler than shots), scaled by this band's topSpeedMPS ratio to U18's as an athletic-development proxy.

iceDecelerationMPS2.citation: mu*g using Alain Hache's puck-on-ice sliding friction coefficient (~0.1, Physics World: https://physicsworld.com/a/physics-on-ice/) and standard gravity (9.81 m/s^2). Real, age-independent physical constant -- the puck doesn't know how old the players are.
